rationale: MTP is the whole story on this model and it is the one lever that genuinely works. Turning it off halves decode (50.62 -> 21.45 tps), and every fixed draft depth from 1 to 8 is worse than the adaptive default: depths 1-6 lose 21-36% decode, and depth 8 only ties adaptive inside noise (49.72 vs 49.47 tps over 9 alternating blocks each). So the default adaptive depth is kept rather than replaced with a hand-picked number, which is the opposite of the Qwen3.8-27B result where depth 6 beat adaptive. KV quantization is a clear rejection: with MTP on, 8-bit costs 5% decode and 21 ms TTFT, 4-bit is inside noise on decode and also 21 ms worse on TTFT, and 4-bit without skip_last does not run at all under MTP. There is no memory argument for it either, since 18.88 GB resident sits far under the ~89.6 GB ceiling. Context window is a genuine no-op at both a 49-token and an ~8k-token prompt, so native 262144 is kept because it is free and accepts prompts a 32768 cap would reject. Sampling is throughput-neutral: the card sampler and a temp-0.2 coding sampler are within 0.6 tps of each other and both produce correct code on all three guardrail prompts, so the coding sampler is kept for determinism. force_sampling is the one sampling knob that costs real throughput (6.6% decode) and is left false. Thinking is the interesting negative result: unlike every other model in this repo, enable_thinking actually works here - the template has a real switch and the model emits genuine reasoning_content - but it costs 15.9 s to the first content token against 0.33 s with it off, a 48x latency penalty that no small coding task can absorb, so it is off. DFlash is unavailable in practice: it is mutually exclusive with MTP, and with MTP off and no draft model configured it is a no-op at 21.71 tps. MoE expert offload does not apply to a dense model and the endpoint correctly returns 400. The final config is therefore the default config with three deliberate changes: thinking pinned off, the coding sampler, and force_sampling off. Its throughput is statistically identical to the defaults (paired A/B: 37.39 vs 37.06 tps, 319.5 vs 316.3 ms TTFT), which is the honest outcome - the performance was already in the MTP default.
failure_modes: turboquant_kv_enabled true with turboquant_kv_bits 4.0 and turboquant_skip_last false is a hard server error under MTP: 'scaled_dot_product_attention(): incompatible function arguments ... Invoked with types: mlx.core.array, mlx_vlm.turboquant._QuantizedStateProxy, mlx_vlm.turboquant._QuantizedStateProxy'. The quantized KV state is passed straight into attention without being materialized. skip_last must stay true whenever KV quant is on.
dflash_enabled true together with mtp_enabled true returns HTTP 400: 'MTP and DFlash cannot both be enabled; choose one speculative-decoding path.'
dflash_enabled true with MTP off and dflash_draft_model null is accepted and loads, but is a no-op: 21.71 tps, indistinguishable from MTP off. There is no DFlash draft model on disk.

moe_expert_offload_enabled does not apply: GET /admin/api/models/gemma-4-31B-it-oQ4e-mtp/moe-offload-fit returns HTTP 400 'Model does not support MoE expert offload'. This is correct for a dense model (enable_moe_block false), not an error to fix.

enable_thinking true works on this model (unlike flint, Qwen3.8-27B and Ornith) but is unusable for interactive coding: 15.9 s to the first content token, and with max_tokens 700 the budget is exhausted by reasoning_content before the answer completes (finish_reason: length).

Changing a reload-requiring setting (mtp_enabled, mtp_adaptive_max_depth, turboquant_kv_enabled, dflash_enabled) unloads the model and auto_unloaded does not reload it. POST /load and poll until loaded: true before measuring. max_context_window and the sampler keys do not reload.

The model reported loaded: true for ~105 s and then unloaded itself with no request in flight. The cause was a server restart by the coordinator, not an idle TTL; no measurement was in flight and nothing was discarded.
measure.py intermittently exits non-zero with no 'run 1:' line; retry up to 3x.
measurement_caveat: Absolute throughput drifted ~30% over this pass (56.1 tps at baseline, 40.06 tps at the final 5-run, with no config change between the two ends of that range). No number here is comparable to a number from a different block. Every verdict is a paired comparison: interleaved A/B for non-reloading knobs (context, sampling, force_sampling), forward+backward ordering for the reload-requiring MTP and KV sweeps, and alternating blocks for the two MTP depth finalists. The baseline and final configs were additionally compared head-to-head in one interleaved A/B (n=6 each) precisely because their separately-measured medians differ by 29% while the paired test shows them equal within 1%.
